newsitem.title: USA: Researcher hikes estimate of Texas natgas reserves.
newsitem.headline: Researcher hikes estimate of Texas natgas reserves.

text.p: A leading energy researcher on Thursday upped his estimates of natural gas reserves in Texas fields and extended projections of the expected life of gas fields in the state.

William Fisher, a researcher at the Bureau of Economic Geology at the University of Texas at Austin, estimated Texas recoverable natural gas reserves at 427 trillion cubic feet (tcf), up from 249 tcf as recently as five years ago.
"The reason for such a change in perception has been...the striking advances of exploration and recovery technology and the vigorous application of technology as a substitite for price," he said.

Overall, Texas natural gas fields have a resource life of an estimated 85 years, with current production levels seen depleting east Texas fields in about 120 years and Gulf coast fields in about 70 years, he said.
"People have been trying to write off the Gulf coast as dead for the last 30 years," he said in a gas gathering conference sponsored by the Texas Railroad Commission.
Fisher said production from Texas fields could rise to 7 tcf in the next decade, up from about 5 tcf to 5.5 tcf now, with prices flat.
